subject: Reserved GPU capacity — term, credits & sensitivity to GPU pricing
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: purchasing@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:14:00 -04:00
Subject: Capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU market movements

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. We're excited about Redwood's latency profile and the autoscale controls. Procurement asked me to share a clear committed-capacity ask so they can model budget and approvals. High level:

- Desired start: 2026-07-01
- Initial reserved pool: 80 A100-equivalent GPUs (in 8-node pools)
- Commit term options we're evaluating: 12 months vs 24 months
- Primary ask: how pricing and any credits would adjust if average GPU spot-equivalent market prices shift down by 15-30% during the term

Attached is a first pass term sheet and our internal cost sensitivity model (acme_gpu_cost_model.xlsx). Two requests from our side:
1) Can you provide a worked example of the unit cost (per token / per GPU-hour) at current pricing and at -15% and -30% GPU market levels?
2) If GPU prices fall materially, are there standard credit / repricing clauses Redwood offers for 12m vs 24m commits?

We need this to get through our procurement committee next week. If helpful, happy to do a brief call with finance.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Acme AI

Attachments: RDW-Acme-term-sheet-v3.pdf, acme_gpu_cost_model.xlsx

Forwarding Acme's ask — they want worked examples and to understand how we handle downward GPU price movement for commit terms. Key points: 80 A100-equivalent (8-node pools), start 7/1, evaluating 12 vs 24 months.

Karthik: can you run our cost model and produce per-GPU-hour and per-1M-token examples at current, -15%, -30% GPU cost scenarios? Highlight where our margin compression hits our approval thresholds.

Ben: from sales/discounting, what flex do we have on credits or retroactive rebates for a 24m vs 12m commit? Any precedent (SOC2 customers, enterprise deals) where we offered mid-term price adjustments?

Laura: finance — if GPU prices drop and we agreed to a rebate or credit, how do we recognize revenue and what approvals would you need? Also include whether we can structure a market-indexed credit rather than a hard repricing clause (easier for us).

I'll offer a short call with Acme next week once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Evelyn

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU market movements

Evelyn / Ben / Laura —

Attached is a short model output I put together from infra's angle (see attachment: rdw_gpu_sensitivity_outlook.xlsx). Summary of the working examples you asked for (assume NPU = normalized A100-equivalent):

- Baseline (current market): unit cost per GPU-hour = $2.40; effective per-1M-token cost (chat workload mix) = $8.50
- If GPU market price -15%: unit cost per GPU-hour = $2.04; per-1M-token = $7.23 (15% reduction)
- If GPU market price -30%: unit cost per GPU-hour = $1.68; per-1M-token = $5.95 (30% reduction)

Notes:
- These figures assume we maintain the same reserved instance utilization (70% avg) and unchanged host overheads (networking, licensing). If utilization improves, per-token cost drops further.
- For 80 A100-equivalent pool, annualized incremental gross margin impact if we pass full market drop through: ~ -$1.2M (for -30%) vs baseline — that is, we would forgo that margin unless we protect via approvals or indexing.
- Short-term mitigation: autoscale + burst off-peak to decrease reserved sizing risk; longer-term: propose a two-tier mechanism (see below).

Suggested approaches (technical / engineering implications):
1) Market-indexed credit: if our GPU procurement index falls > X% over baseline, Redwood credits customer Y% of monthly committed fees for the delta. Operationally this is simple (monthly reconciliation) and preserves accounting simplicity if framed as a credit.
2) Fixed rebate ladder: agree discrete breakpoints (-15%, -30%) with fixed credit amounts. More predictable for customer; requires finance and legal sign-off.
3) No mid-term repricing for 12m; 24m can include an annual repricing clause with cap (e.g., up to 10% pass-through).

I'll attach the spreadsheet I used. Happy to present the numbers in a quick 20m call.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Inference Optimizations (acting)
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: rdw_gpu_sensitivity_outlook.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU market movements

Short answer from GTM: we have room to offer credits but approvals depend on commit length and ARR. Practical proposal:

- 12m commit (80 A100-eq): standard volume discount, no mid-term repricing; we can offer a one-time onboarding credit ($75k) tied to meeting start date and utilization targets.
- 24m commit: offer a market-indexed credit capped at 12% of committed fees annually. Reconciliation quarterly; credit applied to invoices. Requires VP Sales approval for >10% credit and CFO sign-off.

Precedent: we did a similar indexed credit for a fintech customer in 2025 with a 3-tier ladder. Legal asked for clear caps and audit rights.

Ask: Laura — what approvals exactly are needed if we propose up to 12% capped credit? Also would prefer to route any >10% through commercial leadership.

Ben
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU market movements

All — quick finance read on the proposed options.

- Accounting treatment: Market-indexed credits applied to invoices are straightforward; treat as contra-revenue (reduce recognized revenue) when credits are applied. For multi-year deals, we prefer built-in caps and predictable schedules to avoid churn in revenue recognition assumptions.
- Approval thresholds: Commercial can approve up to 10% recurring credit on committed fees; anything >10% requires VP Sales and Finance (me) sign-off; >15% needs CFO. For one-time onboarding credits, <$100k can be approved by Sales ops; >$100k requires Finance Director review.
- Recommendation: Offer Acme two options on the table: 12m with onboarding credit ($75k) OR 24m with market-indexed credit capped at 12% (requires VP Sales sign-off). Structure indexing tied to a neutral GPU price index (we suggest GPUIndex.io) with quarterly reconciliation.

Evelyn — if you can get Acme to agree to the indexing vendor and the cap, I can pre-approve the 12% cap pending VP Sales sign-off; we'll route paperwork for signature.

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Jane — thanks for the detailed packet and model. Internal recap and proposal below.

Option A (12 months):
- Reserved: 80 A100-eq GPUs starting 2026-07-01
- One-time onboarding credit: $75,000 tied to activation and 65%+ utilization in month 1
- No mid-term repricing or credits

Option B (24 months):
- Reserved: 80 A100-eq GPUs starting 2026-07-01
- Market-indexed credit: quarterly reconciliation using GPUIndex.io; credit applied monthly to invoices if the index is below baseline
- Cap on credits: 12% of annual committed fees (requires VP Sales sign-off)

We can also do a hard ladder (e.g., -15% => 6% credit, -30% => 12% credit) if you prefer predictability. Attached is an updated term sheet reflecting the two options (RDW-Acme-term-sheet-v3.pdf) and the internal sensitivity output.

Can you let me know which option Acme prefers by Friday 6/19? If you want a 20m call to walk through the numbers, Ben & Karthik can join.

Best,
Evelyn
